_help.about: [NOT WIRED YET — design §ET] Torchfire 1, the ambient first-person dungeon crawler. The open world is Torchfire 2 and stays in the code, switched off (§ET.2). The game runs unchanged until the code reads this file. First guesses by Claude (chat), 6 Oct; the designer owns them.
_help.opening: §ET.3. You wake underground in a ruin's central room by a lit hearth. exits_min / exits_max: corridors leaving it, each generated from the seed. bundle: unlit torches by the hearth (torch.json bundle, §AW). rescuer: the figure who found you and brought you here (§DE), at the hearth. teach: wordless, no tooltips. first_theme: the theme of the first ruin (a key of themes).
_help.persistence: §ET.10 call 3, Claude's reading, NOT confirmed by Mike: the layout is new each new game (from the seed) and the same within a game; relit lights stay lit; gates keep their state, so a code found later opens a gate passed earlier.
_help.themes: §ET.5. Stage themes, each a ruin of its biome. ruin_kind: the ruins.json / delves.json kind its rooms come from (open where no kind fits yet). air: still or drafty (torch.json snuff.draft). dark: how dark before you relight it. space: tight or exposed. frames: Project-sheet reference frames. Only the two Mike named are listed; §CJ's delve types and the monuments (§DN–§DZ) are the pool for more.
_help.progress: §ET.4. Relit fire-holders (delves.json fire_holders) stay lit for the game and are places to relight a torch. Items are keys, tools and knowledge only (item_kinds): no damage numbers, no rarity, no chests (§CJ.3).
_help.gates: §ET.4. Puzzle gates to rediscover, never traps to punish. kinds: the ones talked through (PSO's obelisk set; a code from a found scroll; a passage that opens once relit). How each works is Claude Code's call within §ET.
_help.sprites: §ET.8. Figures and creatures are sprites baked from the shared rig (painted per §ES). around: directions around the figure (Doom's eight). rows_deg: viewing heights, the camera's elevation above the figure's eye line in degrees (negative is from below); the nearest row is drawn. anim_fps: the sprite animation's own steppy rate; the game still renders at full rate. sprite / geometry: what is and is not a sprite. candidates: small things with no engine shape yet, sprite candidates (first guess).
